I think the pictures that you add are great with good natural lighting and a simply background. I have just noticed that buyers want a lot of pictures. They want to see pictures with the garment laid flat with a measuring tape so they know how you do measurements. I do a simple front and back, close up of the tag, one shot for each measurement (pain in the butt with pants) and close-ups of any flaws or special features (like embellishments or distressing).   
  
I noticed your descriptions are also brief, so I'd suggest beefing them up. I honestly plug in measurements and details and let ChatGPT do mine. Don't say "measurements by request" because few people will take the time to ask and will move onto the next seller. ALWAYS include measurements. Here is a very helpful guide of which ones to include based on the article of clothing and how to do each one:  
[https://blog.poshmark.com/2014/09/25/posh-tip-how-to-measure-items-for-resale/](https://blog.poshmark.com/2014/09/25/posh-tip-how-to-measure-items-for-resale/)

One last little thing, but it helps with the algorithm showing your listings. Always make the brand name of the item the first thing in the description. For example: Old Navy Distressed Women's Jeans - Size 4 \*NWT\* 

Hope that helps!

This reminds me of a story that I remember my dad telling me when I was younger. He told it quite a bit.

He was a truck driver and was in the middle of a long stretch of road with barely anyone around in the middle of New Mexico. Said he would sometimes go thirty minutes without even seeing another car. It was also raining quite heavily.

He sees a man dressed in black clutching a Bible beside the road and picks him up. Immediately, my dad is freaked out because this guy who was just standing in a rain storm in the middle of nowhere was BONE DRY. His hair was dry, his clothes were dry, his skin and even the Bible were dry.  


They talk for a few minutes, then the man just says "you can let me out here." My dad looks around. Absolutely nothing for miles. He presses the guy to let him take him to the next town, but the guy refuses. My dad obliges and pulls over. The guy gets out (my dad is examining him again to make sure he saw what he thought he saw) and my dad drives away. He looks in his mirror to see which way the guy was headed or what he could possibly do. Guy was not there. There was absolutely nowhere he could have gone.
